purpose: Public sequential question/evidence/decision register. Raw experimental assets remain private.

entries.question: Can the Kaggle Gemma environment load the intended model, capture the correct text MLP tensors and preserve execution semantics?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary of preserved engineering runs; not a newly preregistered question.
entries.method: Dependency/model smoke runs, text-versus-media module selection, hook and cache checks; preserve and repair failures.
entries.result: Real text-channel capture became possible after dependency, scope and cache issues. Early failures remain in receipts and compute ledger.
entries.interpretation: Engineering access is necessary but does not identify a functional neuron role.
entries.next_question: Which measured changes correspond to useful behaviour rather than formatting or numerical execution?
entries.direction_decision: Retain the instrumentation; do not repeat smoke tests without a new implementation change or failure.

entries.question: Can verified self-generated code and controlled response-format adaptation produce useful changes in the model?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary; original sources/receipts retain the precise historical conditions.
entries.method: Generate96 solutions, independently verify candidates, compare adaptation objectives and paired activation changes.
entries.result: Accepted 37 of 96 generated solutions, concentrated in two families. On the corrected 12-task development set, the base passed 5 tasks, the full-response adapter passed 6, and the boundary adapter passed 4. No general improvement was established.
entries.interpretation: Data acceptance concentration and response-format confounding require controlled analysis.
entries.next_question: Do position/format effects explain observed activation changes?
entries.direction_decision: Historical training is superseded. Reuse only its infrastructure/lessons; no more adapter training.

entries.question: How do controlled response-position objectives affect activity and development coding scores?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary linked to original result receipt.
entries.method: Position controls, paired prompts/activations and independently graded development code.
entries.result: On 24 development tasks, the base passed 10, the full-response condition passed 14, boundary passed 9, header passed 10, and random passed 11. The full condition had four gains and no losses against base (paired p = 0.125). This was exploratory and inconclusive.
entries.interpretation: Activity drift alone is not useful learning or a functional role.
entries.next_question: Are selected channel groups causally important and more useful than matched random groups?
entries.direction_decision: Move to causal tests; do not optimize these training objectives in the current sprint.

entries.question: Do activation/weight-derived channel groups show reproducible causal coding benefit under ablation?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary of the frozen E02 protocol and complete cross-seed receipts.
entries.method: 338/3380-channel groups, two original adapter seeds, sham and matched random groups; fixed development panels.
entries.result: No replicated steering benefit. A secondary first-seed gain failed to replicate; all conditions remain recorded.
entries.interpretation: Changed channels are not automatically domain-functional units.
entries.next_question: Can native-neuron semantic contrasts and direct causal tests identify bounded functions without training?
entries.direction_decision: Broaden the scientific basis from training-drift groups to native functional localization.

entries.question: Do optimizer-state explanations reproduce the observed weight and activation effects across seeds?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary of frozen diagnostics and replication.
entries.method: Fixed optimizer branches with a second-seed replication and predeclared activation-error criterion.
entries.result: Activation approximation criterion failed at both seeds despite smaller weight differences. No general coding improvement.
entries.interpretation: Optimizer diagnostics did not answer the user's current neuron-function goal.
entries.next_question: Which controls are necessary to distinguish actual neuron effects from numerical effects?
entries.direction_decision: Closed groundwork; no continuation under the hard no-training constraint.

entries.question: Do the frozen historical adaptation conditions transfer to the held-out MBPP panel?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary of the original prospectively frozen confirmation.
entries.method: 128 eligible tasks, five fixed conditions,640 predictions, one frozen host scoring pass.
entries.result: Base56/128; four adapters57,59,56,60. All paired intervals include zero; no reliable positive transfer.
entries.interpretation: The development signal did not establish transfer.
entries.next_question: The new neuron study needs its own prospective fresh confirmation after valid causal and engineering evidence.
entries.direction_decision: CLOSED. Never rerun the scorer, choose edits from these outcomes or reuse its answers for new selection.

entries.question: Can equivalent adapter refactorizations alter execution despite exact repeat/identity controls?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary; frozen protocol and original failed/startup versions preserved.
entries.method: 13 fixed numerical conditions,208 predictions,1820 compact arrays,2460 factor proofs; zero new optimizer updates.
entries.result: Repeat/identity/power-of-two controls exact. Rank permutations perturb some activities/outputs; one development correctness gain is inconclusive.
entries.interpretation: Numerical execution matters; closest prior already reports equivalent-refactorization effects. No novelty or coding improvement claim.
entries.next_question: Can functional neuron edits be validated against exact noops and representation-matched baselines?
entries.direction_decision: Keep the control lesson. Do not let numerical diagnostics displace neuron-function/coding questions.

entries.question: Would fixed causal masks retain their apparent effects under an equivalent numerical refactorization?
entries.question_provenance: Prepared frozen protocol; no GPU results.
entries.method: Prepared fixed-mask numerical crossover; no run in this direction authorized under the current focus.
entries.result: No measurements. Prepared notebooks are not results.
entries.interpretation: Potentially useful diagnostics, but not the strongest current goal.
entries.next_question: Prioritize the human's native-neuron interpretation and direct-edit objective.
entries.direction_decision: Deferred; do not launch simply because source exists.

entries.question: Can native E2B MLP neurons be localized and steered in a controlled patch-choice pilot, and can silent new-neuron/residual-MLP additions preserve actual-model behaviour?
entries.question_provenance: Question summarized from the prospective N01 protocol, frozen before GPU outputs; subsequent no-training scope amendment changed no runtime conditions.
entries.method: 32 discovery prompts and 64 development prompts; 43 fixed conditions and 2,320 decisions. Individual/group gains, random controls, counterfactual patches and silent 8-neuron/64-unit branches. Zero optimizer updates.
entries.result: All 2,320 rows were checked on the host. Both additions preserved all 64 baseline logit hashes. Identity, cached-generation, reload and restoration checks passed within the receipt limits. Runtime: 961.74 seconds; peak allocated CUDA memory: 7.77 GiB; compact output: 18.02 MB.
entries.interpretation: Actual checkpoint compatibility for these two branch forms is established. Physical dense add/delete, full decoder insertion, individual semantic roles and fresh coding improvement are not established.
entries.next_question: Can matched neurons be compared across original floating-point and NF4 representations, and can prescribed permanent edits pass the same engineering and functional controls?
entries.direction_decision: Go deeper on provenance, precision pairing and direct connection surgery. Broaden beyond binary patch choice before a coding-capability claim.

entries.experiment: N02: shared-source precision and physical surgery
entries.question: Can text-only E2B run in unquantized BF16 and same-parent NF4, and can physical deletion, cloning, prescribed addition and permanent connection edits pass explicit equivalence/reload checks?
entries.question_provenance: Direct human request, developed into the N02 protocol and frozen before GPU outputs. Versions 2 and 3 repair inventory and diagnostic logging under dated amendments; conditions and tolerances are unchanged.
entries.method: Two representations of the same pinned floating-point parent. Fourteen conditions on 16 reused development prompts per representation, plus 12 reload measurements: 460 measurements in total. Zero training. Fixed algebra tolerances and exact identity/restoration gates. NF4 physical edits use an explicitly dequantized target MLP and its unchanged dense baseline;the original-to-dense numerical change is recorded separately.
entries.result: Version 3 completed all 460 measurements across unquantized BF16 and same-parent NF4. All hard gates and ten algebra comparisons passed. Deletion matched zeroing, and outgoing-weight doubling matched gain-2 steering exactly on all 16 prompts in each representation. Physical zero-output addition preserved the dense target-layer baseline exactly. BF16 split cloning changed some logits by up to 0.125 but passed the fixed tolerance and preserved top-1 tokens. Peak allocated CUDA memory was 8.95 GiB (BF16) and 7.00 GiB (NF4). Both startup failures remain recorded.
entries.interpretation: Physical editing and custom patch replay now work on the actual pinned text model in both representations within the tested scope:one channel in layer 34 and 16 development prompts. This does not establish a neuron function, new capability, coding improvement or speedup.
entries.next_question: Can a bounded causal neuron role survive changed wording/output formats and transfer to executable coding?
entries.direction_decision: Engineering gate passed. Move to the functional coding study;retain exact and tolerance-qualified comparisons without rerunning N02.

entries.question: Do the N01 selected channels show a specific coding role or mainly change patch-choice confidence?
entries.question_provenance: Posthoc question and contrast plan recorded after all N01 outcomes were read. No prospective semantic claim.
entries.method: Use all existing conditions and selected traces. Compute coordinate overlap, balanced semantic/label/order contrasts, all9 counterfactual comparisons and random-activity matching quality. No model forwards or final data.
entries.result: The three selected counterfactual groups changed margins but produced no answer-choice flips across 48 recipient prompts. Boundary and deduplication groups shared 4 of 8 channels and the same top-ranked channel. Across 48 random-control matches, the median control/selected activity-RMS ratio was 0.102; none were within 10% of the selected activity RMS. All contrasts and controls are retained.
entries.interpretation: N01 does not identify a domain-specific neuron function or establish coding benefit. Margin effects alone are insufficient.
entries.next_question: Can localization at intermediate semantic/code-continuation positions survive new output formats and actual executable coding tests?
entries.direction_decision: Broaden beyond A/Bdecision-token screening. Use closer activity/effect-size controls in the next functional study; do not relabel the pilot as successful interpretation.

entries.question: Do native neurons conditionally support inclusive-boundary coding across reversed comparison forms, and can fixed edits affect executable completions without damaging retention?
entries.question_provenance: Intent followed the N01 control analysis. The exact N03 protocol was frozen before task implementation and GPU outcomes. The host analysis plan was recorded after launch and before retrieving any outputs.
entries.method: Freeze BF16 discovery selection, activity-matched random controls, same-source NF4 coordinate transfer, real-model token-path checks, identity and semantic/self patches. Test every condition on generated Python line completions and division/JSON retention. No training.
entries.result: All 896 outputs and grades passed the host audit. Every condition scored 4/16 threshold, 4/8 division and 8/8 JSON in each representation. No semantic-patch success change or coding gain occurred. All no-op and restoration checks passed.
entries.interpretation: The selected neurons affect internal scores but do not establish a semantic role. Most dominant threshold outputs were outside the token contrast; development wording also omitted explicit integer types. Shared-KV path controls and current/all-position equivalence passed.
entries.next_question: Can typed tasks and a new fixed memory connection reveal native-neuron functions beyond late output readout?
entries.direction_decision: Broaden. Preserve the null and frozen grades. Verify task clarity and connection feasibility before another localization matrix.

entries.question: Can a clean public code checkout reconstruct every released physical edit from the pinned base and match the original weights and development outputs?
entries.question_provenance: Prospective reconstruction check after the human requested saved edited models on GitHub;not a new coding-benefit experiment.
entries.method: Reconstruct all six fixed physical edits in each representation from the published code and pinned base. Compare all available weight hashes and the original outputs on two unchanged N02 development prompts. No new model selection or training.
entries.result: All 24 original output hashes and all 18 previously recorded projection hashes matched exactly. All 36 edited projection hashes are saved in the model bundles. Zero optimizer updates. A separate full-model replay of the N01 public loader remains unverified.
entries.interpretation: The public package reconstructs the N02 models in the pinned T4 environment. This verifies reconstruction, not a semantic role, coding improvement or bitwise portability across platforms.
entries.next_question: Which native neurons compute useful coding distinctions, and can controlled direct edits improve executable outcomes?
entries.direction_decision: Close R01. Return to N03 functional coding. Further routine reconstruction runs are unnecessary.

entries.experiment: N04: typed coding and memory-connection gate
entries.question: Can a prescribed new memory connection make late native neuron activity causally available to later positions and affect typed coding without training?
entries.question_provenance: Proposed after N03 complete null. The GPU protocol was frozen after 30 random-weight CPU cases and task/oracle preflight, before GPU outcomes.
entries.method: Copy full-attention key/value projections from layer 14 into a frozen memory branch at layer 24. Compare nine fixed policies, historical versus current-only values, feature-permuted controls, typed executable continuations, native-neuron interventions and measurement gradients. No training.
entries.result: All 288 records passed the host audit, including 32 carried original outputs, 32 exact off-mode rows, 18 amended cache checks, 54 path interventions, 18 gradient records and 9 restorations. Historical connections make the tested late native activity affect later outputs; original, off and current-only controls retain the exact past-path null. Full K/V and value replacements score zero on all 32 inputs. Quarter-strength key-only gains two of eight division completions with no observed losses; the unadjusted paired p value is 0.5.
entries.interpretation: The architecture changes access to past native activity without training. This is a structural result, not a semantic neuron role. The small key-only effect reuses four function-name pairs and is unconfirmed across multiple conditions. The typed baseline improves on N03 because prompts changed; that is not a model-edit gain. Cache equivalence remains qualified by the weaker dated diagnostic.
entries.next_question: Which native channels transmit a rounding requirement at a shared instruction anchor, and do necessity, opposite-policy patches and rescue change executable function behavior beyond matched random groups?
entries.direction_decision: Close the connection engineering gate and retain the complete grid. Do not select a winning permutation or strength. Move to early native-neuron functional localization; any later connection benefit test must be prospective and retain mild controls.

entries.experiment: N05: native semantic-anchor roles and executable functions
entries.question: Can a small native neuron group at an instruction anchor transmit a rounding policy and causally change correct function behavior without training?
entries.question_provenance: Proposed after the complete N03 and N04 audits. N03 missed dominant alternatives and selected late units. N04 opens their historical path but does not establish a semantic role.
entries.method: Use forward activity at the same punctuation token in six crossed policy strata to select 32 native channels in layers 0 through 13, with nested eight-channel diagnostics and two strict matched random groups. Test 13 fixed policies on 24 new complete-function and retention prompts, plus 24 descriptive discovery outputs. No fitted vectors, measurement gradients or optimizer updates.
entries.result: All 336 outputs, 48 self/rescue rows, 26 restorations and exact identity controls passed the host audit. The baseline scored 1/16 rounding functions, 4/4 filters and 0/4 strict JSON. Every nonidentity condition scored 0/16, 4/4 and 0/4. Selected and matched random interventions caused the same single loss. No role or gain was established.
entries.interpretation: Nine baseline rounding outputs hit the ceiling and fourteen failed the source/execution gate. Baseline JSON values were correct inside forbidden outer fences; this posthoc content diagnostic leaves the strict grades unchanged. Activity contrast did not establish policy transmission. The missing full-vector anchor control and poor baseline prevent a broad conclusion about native neuron function.
entries.next_question: Can a counterbalanced selector task produce reliable executable expressions, and can full native state transplantation at the selector actually change policy before sparse localization?
entries.direction_decision: Broaden and require a prospective baseline-usability gate plus full-state positive controls. Do not repeat or enlarge the sparse punctuation-anchor sweep. Preserve source/format/cap limitations and every null.

entries.experiment: N06: baseline usability and causal-site gate
entries.question: Can a usable counterbalanced mode selector control executable expressions, and is its information causally accessible through full MLP or reused attention-memory states?
entries.question_provenance: Proposed after N05 complete audit and structure diagnosis. It replaces an inadequate full-function assay and adds the missing full-state positive control.
entries.method: Counterbalanced red/blue integer-filter expressions. Gate usable baseline first, then joint full native MLP or reuse-only K/V donor replacements. Same-policy mapping reversal controls label meaning. No sparse localization yet.
entries.result: All 200 outputs and guards passed. Baseline filtering was correct on 16/16 and JSON on 4/4. Joint early-MLP opposite donors transferred all sixteen programs to the opposite policy. Reversed-mapping same-policy donors preserved fourteen of sixteen. Keys, values and joint K/V produced no functional flips. No outputs hit the cap.
entries.interpretation: Joint early MLP opposite donors transfer16/16;reversed-mapping same-policy donors preserve14/16. K/V donors produce no functional flips. All JSON4/4 and no caps. This locates a conditional site, not individual neuron meanings or coding improvement. Four crossed instruction strata with nuisance-name replications, not sixteen algorithms.
entries.next_question: Which individual layers carry the joint early-MLP effect, and where is native-channel localization justified?
entries.direction_decision: Deepen at the measured MLP site. Decompose every early layer with both donor controls before a sparse search. Opposite-policy transfer is control, not coding improvement.
entries.decision: The proposed rounding assay changed to filtering because N05 filter controls were correct on four of four inputs while rounding was correct on one of sixteen. This is a prospective new assay. N05 grades are unchanged.

entries.experiment: N07: individual-layer decomposition of the native MLP site
entries.question: Which of the fourteen early native MLP layers is sufficient for policy transfer beyond a reversed-mapping same-policy donor control?
entries.question_provenance: Proposed after the complete N06 all-condition audit. The joint early-MLP site transfers every tested opposite policy while keys and values do not.
entries.method: All fourteen individual layers, opposite and same-policy actual donors, exact carried original predictions, live original replay, per-layer self hashes and exact restoration. No sparse selection or optimization.
entries.result: All 600 records passed audit, including twenty carried originals, 280 self hashes, twenty identity generations and sixty restorations. Layer 0 switched all sixteen filter programs under both opposite-rule and same-rule donors. Layers 4 and 9 each switched two prompts under opposite donors only, in a single direction/mapping stratum. Other individual-layer donor conditions preserved all sixteen. All JSON controls passed, with no caps.
entries.interpretation: The layer 0 effect fails the reversed-label same-policy control. No individual layer meets the fixed eligibility criterion. This supports conditional label dependence at the tested whole-layer site, not an abstract-rule neuron or coding improvement.
entries.next_question: Can later-layer blocks specifically rescue a fixed label-corruption background using same-rule donor states?
entries.direction_decision: Follow the prospective branch for no eligible layer: fixed block decomposition and counterfactual rescue. Do not choose layer 0 as an abstract semantic site or rank sparse units blindly.

entries.experiment: N08: fixed-block decomposition and conditional rescue
entries.question: Do later native MLP blocks provide rule-specific rescue after a fixed layer 0 label corruption?
entries.question_provenance: Proposed after the complete N07 audit under its predeclared no-eligible-layer branch. Joint early-layer swaps transfer policies, but layer 0 alone follows the label even under a same-rule donor.
entries.method: Six fixed contiguous blocks in layers 1 through 13. Clean opposite/same-rule swaps and a common layer 0 label-corruption background with opposite, same-rule and recipient donors. Sixty existing reference records are carried without completion regeneration.
entries.result: Three actual tiny-Gemma composition tests and all 660 assignment routes passed. N08 version 1 is running privately with a frozen protocol and auditor. No N08 outputs have been read.
entries.interpretation: This tests conditional block sufficiency and contextual compensation. It cannot by itself identify sparse neuron meanings or establish useful coding improvement.
entries.next_question: Does any prescribed block pass a fixed rescue-specificity criterion, warranting native-channel necessity/rescue?
entries.direction_decision: Freeze before code. Keep every block/control and stop interpretation on any failed identity or restoration guard.
